curation.lead:
Martin L. Edelman (b. 1942) is a veteran New York real estate and corporate attorney who has become the primary legal intermediary between Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth apparatus and American business, technology, and political interests. A Princeton '63 and Columbia Law '66 graduate who began his career writing speeches for Attorney General Robert Kennedy and served in Vietnam, Edelman has been Of Counsel at Paul Hastings LLP since approximately 1992 and a partner at Fisher Brothers. [Finding #4028] Since 2002, when he accompanied U.S. General Tommy Franks on a Gulf tour and met Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, Edelman has accumulated an extraordinary density of roles within Abu Dhabi's sovereign ecosystem: General Counsel of G42, Board Director of MGX, Senior Adviser to Mubadala Investment Company, Board Director of GlobalFoundries (Mubadala designee since 2017), Board Director of City Football Group and Vice Chairman of NYC FC (since 2008), Executive Chairman of Manchester Life, Board of Trustees member at MBZUAI, Director of Aldar REIT, and adviser to Royal Group. [Finding #3984] [Finding #4028]

Edelman simultaneously maintains a longstanding personal friendship with Donald Trump dating to the 1980s New York City real estate era. [Finding #4034] This dual positioning -- trusted adviser to Abu Dhabi royals and personal friend of a sitting U.S. president -- made Edelman the natural intermediary for the transaction that has drawn the most scrutiny: in January 2025, he and G42 CEO Peng Xiao signed the agreement through which Aryam Investment 1, an entity controlled by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, acquired 49 percent of World Liberty Financial (WLFI), the Trump family cryptocurrency venture, for $500 million. Edelman and Peng Xiao received two of five WLFI board seats, though neither was listed on WLFI's public team page. [Finding #4125] [Finding #4038]

Separately, Edelman appears in the Jeffrey Epstein documentary record. He was scheduled on Epstein's calendar for December 16, 2016 -- the same day Leon Black had a 10 a.m. appointment -- and his identity was confirmed through an email exchange between Epstein's assistant Lesley Groff and scientist Martin Nowak. [Finding #4031] Six months later, on June 24, 2017, Epstein emailed a contact identified as "Jabor Y." with the subject line "legal advice for MBZ" and a link to Edelman's AMD board appointment press release. [Finding #4030] Edelman also appeared on Epstein's master contact lists in October and November 2016, and on a June 2019 list titled "list for bannon steve" alongside Gulf contacts and political names. [Finding #4032]
curation.system_role: Edelman represents the archetype of a private-sector legal intermediary who accumulates simultaneous fiduciary, advisory, and board positions across an entire sovereign wealth ecosystem, then deploys that accumulated access to broker transactions between foreign state capital and domestic political interests -- without public disclosure of the full scope of overlapping roles, and with documented proximity to Jeffrey Epstein during the period when Epstein was seeking access to the same Abu Dhabi power structure.

sections.title: Abu Dhabi Sovereign Network
sections.content:
Edelman's entry into the Abu Dhabi sovereign apparatus traces to 2002, when he accompanied U.S. Central Command commander General Tommy Franks on a tour of Gulf states. Franks, who was overseeing operations in Afghanistan and preparing for the Iraq invasion, visited Arab leaders monthly. Through these military-facilitated introductions, Edelman built relationships with Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed (now UAE President) and his brother Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed (now UAE National Security Adviser). [Finding #4029] He initially also worked in Libya with Gaddafi's son but shifted his focus to Abu Dhabi as Libya's situation destabilized. He was reportedly granted Emirati citizenship, an extremely rare distinction for a foreign national. [Finding #4029]

Over the following two decades, Edelman accumulated an unusually dense portfolio of positions within institutions controlled or influenced by the Al Nahyan family. He serves as General Counsel of G42, the artificial intelligence company chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon; Board Director of MGX, Tahnoon's AI-focused investment fund; Senior Adviser to Mubadala Investment Company, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund; Mubadala's designee on the board of GlobalFoundries (the semiconductor manufacturer, since February 2017, preceded by a similar designee role on the AMD board from 2013 to 2017); Board Director and Vice Chairman of City Football Group (the entity that owns Manchester City FC, since September 2008); Executive Chairman of Manchester Life (the Abu Dhabi joint venture real estate development in Manchester); Board of Trustees member at Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI); Director of Aldar REIT; adviser to Royal Group (Tahnoon's personal conglomerate); and a member of the Sky News Arabia Editorial Advisory Committee. [Finding #3984] [Finding #4028] [Finding #4051]

The pattern is consistent: wherever Abu Dhabi sovereign capital enters Western markets -- sports (Manchester City, NYCFC, UFC), education (NYU Abu Dhabi, MBZUAI), technology (AMD, GlobalFoundries, G42, MGX), media (Sky News Arabia), and real estate (Aldar, Manchester Life) -- Edelman holds a governance or advisory role. [Finding #4051] He led the negotiations with the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security and National Security Council on G42's divestiture of Chinese technology partnerships, working alongside Peng Xiao, Tahnoon, and UAE Ambassador Yousef Al Otaiba. Paul Hastings LLP, where Edelman remains Of Counsel, advised G42 on its $1.5 billion strategic investment from Microsoft. [Finding #3857]

Edelman also facilitated the introduction that led to Sheikh Tahnoon's approximately $200 million investment in UFC. Per a New Yorker profile of Ari Emanuel, "Emanuel called a New York real-estate lawyer named Martin Edelman, whom he had met through representing the UFC. Edelman was a longtime adviser to the Fertitta brothers. More important, he was close to the royal family of the Emirates." Edelman introduced Emanuel to Khaldoon Al Mubarak, and approximately one year later, Tahnoon made a handshake deal with Lorenzo Fertitta for ten percent of UFC. [Finding #4033]

sections.title: Trump Relationship and World Liberty Financial
sections.content:
Bloomberg reported in May 2025 that Edelman holds "strong ties with figures across the spectrum -- from the Kennedy family and George Soros to a longstanding friendship with Donald Trump, dating back to their 1980s real estate days." [Finding #4034] This friendship, rooted in the New York City real estate world where both men operated for decades, gained geopolitical significance when Edelman helped organize Trump's May 2025 visit to Abu Dhabi, during which the United States and UAE signed a strategic AI partnership including a five-gigawatt computing and energy hub. [Finding #4034]

The most consequential deployment of Edelman's dual access came on January 16, 2025 -- four days before the presidential inauguration -- when he and G42 CEO Peng Xiao signed the agreement through which Aryam Investment 1 acquired 49 percent of World Liberty Financial for $500 million. Edelman signed in his capacity as G42 General Counsel. At least $187 million of the initial payment flowed to Trump family entities DT Marks DEFI LLC and DT Marks SC LLC. Edelman and Peng Xiao received two of five WLFI board seats, but neither was listed on WLFI's public-facing team page. [Finding #4125] [Finding #4038]

The transaction placed Edelman at the intersection of a congressional inquiry. In February 2026, Representative Ro Khanna launched a probe into whether the WLFI investment influenced U.S. policy on AI chip export controls to the UAE. Edelman's simultaneous roles as G42 General Counsel (representing Tahnoon's technology interests), MGX Board Director (overseeing Tahnoon's AI investment fund), GlobalFoundries Board member (sitting on the board of a Mubadala-owned semiconductor manufacturer), Paul Hastings Of Counsel (with attorney-client privilege concerns), and WLFI board member (representing Aryam's stake in the Trump crypto venture) mean that he straddles multiple sides of the regulatory question under investigation. [Finding #4038]

sections.title: Epstein Documentary Record
sections.content:
Three categories of evidence place Edelman in Jeffrey Epstein's documentary record, all dating from 2016 to 2019.

First, Edelman was scheduled on Epstein's calendar for December 16, 2016, noted as "TBD Martin Edelman." The same day, Leon Black had a 10 a.m. appointment. An email chain from December 8, 2016, shows Epstein's assistant Lesley Groff initially contacted Harvard scientist Martin Nowak about the meeting, confusing the two Martins. When Nowak replied "could it be someone else (not me)?", Groff realized "perhaps the person full name IS Martin Edelman!!" This exchange confirms the calendar entry referred to Martin L. Edelman the attorney, not any scientist. [Finding #4031] (EFTA02665747, EFTA02346158)

Second, on June 24, 2017, Epstein emailed a recipient identified as "Jabor Y." from his personal account (jeevacation@gmail.com) with the subject line "legal advice for MBZ" and a link to a press release announcing Edelman's appointment to the AMD board of directors. [Finding #4030] (EFTA02645374) "MBZ" is Mohammed bin Zayed, now President of the UAE. The email was sent after Epstein's 2008 conviction and during a period when Epstein was actively rebuilding his network. Whether Epstein was recommending Edelman as counsel to Abu Dhabi figures, or was sharing intelligence about Edelman's role in Abu Dhabi governance, remains an open question. [Finding #4054]

Third, Edelman appeared on Epstein's master contact lists. On October 30 and November 1, 2016, Epstein sent himself lists containing names organized by category; "Edelman" appears in the first section, followed by "set martin, Lata, susskind, strominger..." mixing scientists with political and financial contacts including "kerry, clinton, richardson, mapp, leahy, spitzer, schumer." A later version from June 30, 2019, titled "list for bannon steve," includes "pritzker edelman. set lloyd, martin novak" alongside Gulf contacts "raafat, sultan hamad jabor." [Finding #4032] (EFTA02445902, EFTA02446049, HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_029622) The juxtaposition of Edelman with both Steve Bannon and Gulf contacts in the 2019 list suggests Epstein viewed Edelman as a combined political and Gulf access point.

sections.title: Institutional Continuity: Epstein to WLFI
sections.content:
The most structurally significant pattern in the Edelman record is the continuity between the Abu Dhabi sovereign infrastructure that Epstein sought to penetrate in 2017 and the same infrastructure that now funds Trump family ventures. In June 2017, Epstein emailed "Jabor Y." about "legal advice for MBZ," referencing Edelman. [Finding #4030] (EFTA02645374) In a separate communication, Epstein told David Stern to convey to MBZ that "he should meet with me about digital currency." [Finding #4285] (EFTA02589631)

The institutions Epstein was seeking access to -- G42, Royal Group, Mubadala -- are the same institutions through which the WLFI deal was executed in January 2025. The intermediary is the same person: Martin Edelman. Over the intervening years, Edelman accumulated twelve or more positions within the Tahnoon-controlled ecosystem, and it was in his capacity as G42 General Counsel that he signed the $500 million Aryam-WLFI agreement. [Finding #4285]

This does not establish that Epstein caused or facilitated the current deals. But it demonstrates infrastructure continuity: the relational pathways between Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth and American political-financial interests that Epstein attempted to exploit in 2017 remained intact and functional in 2025, with the same bridge figure in place. Edelman is the only documented individual who simultaneously has connections to Epstein (calendar, contact lists, and the "legal advice for MBZ" email), to Sheikh Tahnoon (as G42 General Counsel, MGX board member, and Royal Group adviser), and to Donald Trump (personal friendship since the 1980s) -- while also serving as the signatory on the WLFI deal that connected these networks financially. [Finding #4098]

sections.title: Corporate Registry and Financial Records
sections.content:
Corporate registry records reveal that Edelman held officer positions in multiple Florida hotel corporations during the 1990s, all using the address 280 Park Avenue or 75 East 55th Street, New York. These entities -- Key West Florida Hotel Corp, Lake Park Florida Hotel Corp, Coral Gables Florida Hotel Corp, FGS Florida Hotel Corp, New Galahad West Corp, New Maitland Corp, New Intracoastal A Corp, and RCC Property Advisors Inc -- appear to be connected to Chartwell Hotels Associates, which Edelman's LittleSis profile lists as a partnership he held. The 75 East 55th Street address is Fisher Brothers' Park Avenue Plaza. [Finding #4040]

SEC records confirm Edelman holds CIK 0001047252 with more than 212 insider transaction filings, primarily Form 4s related to GlobalFoundries (GFS) stock transactions. Form 144 (intent to sell) filings in December 2023 indicate ongoing disposition of GlobalFoundries shares. [Finding #4036] His FEC political donation record is notably modest for a figure of his influence: two donations totaling $5,000 to Senator Chris Coons (D-DE) in July 2025. [Finding #4036] The National Law Journal named him one of 34 most influential lawyers in the United States in 2011, and he received the Department of the Army Public Service Award in 2007, a recognition that post-dates his 2002 Gulf tour with General Franks by five years. [Finding #4036] [Finding #4028]

open_questions: What was the nature of the December 16, 2016 meeting between Edelman and Epstein? Was it a one-time encounter or part of an ongoing relationship, and did any business, advisory, or Gulf-related discussion take place -- particularly given that Leon Black had a separate appointment with Epstein the same day?

Who is 'Jabor Y.,' the recipient of Epstein's June 2017 email about 'legal advice for MBZ' referencing Edelman? Is this Jabor bin Yousuf Al Serkal, another UAE figure, or someone connected to Qatar's Al Thani family? Identifying this recipient would clarify whether Epstein had independent access to Abu Dhabi leadership or was seeking to build it through Edelman.

Did Edelman know about or facilitate any contact between Epstein and Abu Dhabi principals (Tahnoon, MBZ, Khaldoon Al Mubarak), or was Epstein's interest in Edelman's Abu Dhabi roles conducted without Edelman's knowledge or involvement?

What conflict-of-interest review, if any, was conducted before Edelman simultaneously took a WLFI board seat (representing Abu Dhabi's investment in a U.S. president's crypto venture) while serving as G42 General Counsel, MGX Board Director, GlobalFoundries Board member, and Paul Hastings Of Counsel?

Does Edelman's reported Emirati citizenship create any legal obligations -- such as reporting requirements under UAE law or potential FARA implications in the United States -- that would be relevant to his role as intermediary in transactions between UAE sovereign entities and Trump family businesses?
